### A Brewer's Good Year

By Bay Tribune Business

---

In Uptown, the year closed well for Kwame Fitzgerald. The craft-brewery owner took on increased responsibilities this cycle — the kind of quiet step up that never makes a headline but tells you a small business has found its footing. At Thanksgiving, in a city breathing a little easier, it reads like the season itself: not a windfall, just a good year, earned one pour at a time.

### Query: "Oakland business economic Stabilization Fund development"

"Holiday weekends here, we don't slow down," Campbell said. "But I grew up closer to West Oakland and the energy is different over there. People want to spend. There's just less to spend it on." The fund's architecture targets three categories: lease stabilization grants for existing businesses facing rent escalation, capital improvement micro-loans for facade and equipment upgrades, and corridor activation grants designed to attract new tenants to long-vacant commercial spaces. City economic development staff have signaled that lease stabilization will be the first tranche, given urgency around several pending rent renegotiations along the Seventh Street corridor. What the investment pipeline looks like from here matters. The holiday weekend proved again that Oakland has the consumer demand — Jack London and Uptown posted some of their strongest evening numbers of the year, with multiple nightlife venues in both districts reporting capacity crowds.

------------------------------------------------------------ BUSINESS TICKER By Jordan Velez, Bay Tribune Business The West Oakland Stabilization Fund's authorization bottleneck has not cleared. Forty-seven families are approved. Zero checks have been delivered. Mayor Santana has now issued a direct authorization for disbursements within ten days. Beverly Hayes, the home health aide from West Oakland who was approved for $18,500 and has been waiting, should finally get her money. Deputy Mayor Brenda Okoro is now reviewing every application that exceeds the standard timeline. OEWD Director Marcus Webb has been asked to explain in writing why the authorization gate jammed. The two hundred ninety-five applications still in queue will move through a two-week rolling review process beginning immediately.
